skill.name: trigger-dev
skill.description: Guidance for designing Trigger.dev background jobs, AI workflows, scheduled tasks, webhooks, queues, and reliable TypeScript async execution.
skill.summary: Build reliable Trigger.dev tasks and workflows for TypeScript applications.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive caused by Markdown inline code formatting in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable behavior was found in the reviewed skill content.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 67 uses Markdown backticks to format related skill names, not Ruby or shell command execution. The file is prompt-only guidance and contains no executable code path.

content.value_statement: Background jobs can fail when retries, payloads, and deployment details are unclear. This skill guides Trigger.dev task design for reliable TypeScript workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides Trigger.dev task setup for TypeScript and Next.js projects.
Explains AI background jobs that use built-in integration patterns.
Covers scheduled triggers, webhook handlers, task queues, and batch processing.
Highlights timeout, payload serialization, environment variable, and SDK version risks.
Recommends idempotency keys, logging, and concurrency limits for safer task execution.
limitations: Does not include runnable source files or generated project scaffolding.
Requires project details, Trigger.dev version, and deployment target for precise advice.
Does not make live API calls or verify cloud configuration automatically.
May need current Trigger.dev documentation for version-specific behavior.

use_cases.title: Plan Production Background Tasks
use_cases.description: Design reliable Trigger.dev tasks with clear payloads, retries, logging, and timeout rules before implementation.

use_cases.title: Move AI Workflows Out Of Requests
use_cases.description: Convert long-running AI processing into background jobs that can retry and report progress cleanly.

use_cases.title: Review Async Deployment Risks
use_cases.description: Check queues, environment variables, SDK versions, and concurrency settings before shipping Trigger.dev workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Start A Background Job
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a Trigger.dev background job for this task: [describe task]. Include payload shape, retry behavior, and logging needs.

prompt_templates.title: Design An AI Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Trigger.dev AI workflow that runs for several minutes. Cover steps, failure handling, progress updates, and safe retries.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Trigger.dev Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Trigger.dev task plan for production risks. Focus on timeouts, idempotency, serialization, environment variables, and concurrency.

prompt_templates.title: Architect A Multi-Service Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Trigger.dev pipeline that coordinates multiple external services. Include queue strategy, batching, retry boundaries, and duplicate side-effect prevention.

output_examples.input: Design a job that processes uploaded documents with an AI model.
output_examples.output: A staged task plan with document validation, AI processing, progress reporting, retry policy, timeout guidance, and idempotency checks.

output_examples.input: Review a scheduled sync that calls several partner APIs.
output_examples.output: A reliability review covering schedule design, API rate limits, queue concurrency, duplicate updates, logging, and deployment configuration.

output_examples.input: Move a webhook handler into a background workflow.
output_examples.output: A workflow outline that validates the webhook quickly, enqueues durable work, tracks retries, and protects downstream side effects.

best_practices: Use small focused tasks with explicit payloads and clear retry boundaries.
Add idempotency keys before tasks call payment, email, or external write APIs.
Set timeouts, logging, and queue concurrency limits before production rollout.
anti_patterns: Putting every workflow step into one large task without checkpoints.
Passing non-serializable payloads or hidden process state into tasks.
Allowing retries to repeat external side effects without safeguards.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps design Trigger.dev background jobs, AI workflows, scheduled tasks, webhooks, queues, and batch processes.

faq.question: Does it generate runnable code?
faq.answer: It provides implementation guidance and task structure, but the skill file does not include runnable source code.

faq.question: Can it help with Next.js projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explicitly covers Trigger.dev setup patterns for Next.js and TypeScript applications.

faq.question: Can it review reliability risks?
faq.answer: Yes. It focuses on timeouts, retries, idempotency, logging, environment variables, SDK versions, and concurrency limits.

faq.question: Does it require Trigger.dev cloud access?
faq.answer: No. It can provide planning and review guidance without accessing your Trigger.dev account.
